name: Consistency regularization: reversal KL (p(x) vs Rev(p(x_rev))) + cross-lingual view-agreement KL
links: Li et al. 2019, 'A Logic-Driven Framework for Consistency of Neural Models', EMNLP (arXiv:1909.00126; code github.com/utahnlp/consistency); Zheng et al. 2021, 'Consistency Regularization for Cross-Lingual Fine-Tuning' (xTune), ACL (arXiv:2106.08226; code github.com/bozheng-hit/xTune); Asai & Hajishirzi 2020, 'Logic-Guided Data Augmentation and Regularization for Consistent Question Answering', ACL (arXiv:2004.10157; github.com/AkariAsai/logic_guided_qa); Minervini & Riedel 2018 (ACL) adversarial logic regularisation for NLI; R-Drop (Liang et al. 2021, NeurIPS) for dropout-view symmetric KL. Task: https://inigolopezgazpio.net/SemEval-2027-Task-2-DiCo-NLI/
license_access: Method only; reference code releases are MIT/Apache-style open source [uncertain]. Works with any open-weight backbone.
track_coverage: Reversal KL: all tracks (T1-T4). Cross-lingual view KL: needs the same source pair in several languages, which the training data provides via shared pair_id across T1/T2/T3/T4, so it is most natural when training a single multilingual model on all tracks jointly (serving T2, T3, T4 especially). For a T1-only English model it reduces to reversal KL (plus optional R-Drop).
basque_quality: Indirectly helpful: the view-agreement term distils the (typically more accurate) EN/ES predictions into the EU view of the same source pair. xTune shows the largest gains on lower-resource/distant languages (XNLI: Urdu +5.4, Swahili +2.2 over XLM-R-large in zero-shot transfer; cross-lingual transfer gap reduced from 10.6 to 6.9 points with MT augmentation + example consistency). No Basque-specific numbers exist for this regulariser [uncertain].
cross_lingual_robustness: Directly targets the monolingual-vs-mixed gap: forcing p(en-eu view) ~ p(en-en view) ~ p(eu-eu view) of the same pair makes predictions language-invariant. xTune reports more language-invariant representations (Tatoeba retrieval 79.7 -> 82.0 from example consistency on translation pairs). Expect a noticeably smaller T4-vs-T1 gap than plain multi-track fine-tuning [uncertain]. Caveat: translations of some phrase pairs are not perfectly relation-preserving; the organizers filtered relation-unstable items, which reduces but may not remove this label noise.
architecture: Loss-level method on top of any classifier producing 4-way probabilities p(.|a,b) in LABELS order (EQ, FE, BE, NEG). Total loss L = CE(all views) + lambda_rev * L_rev + lambda_xl * L_xl (+ optional lambda_rd * R-Drop). (1) Reversal term: L_rev = KL_S( p(a,b) || p(b,a)[REVERSE_PERM] ), symmetric KL with stop-gradient on each target side as in xTune (KL(sg(P)||Q) + KL(sg(Q)||P)); alternative Li et al. form |log p_y(a,b) - log p_Rev(y)(b,a)| (product t-norm). Applies to reversible twins and to synthetic swaps of NEG singletons. (2) Cross-lingual term: for the V views of a source pair (EN-EN, ES-ES, EU-EU and 6 mixed combos, all mapped into the canonical 'original' orientation via REVERSE_PERM for flipped views), L_xl = mean_v KL( sg(p_bar) || p_v ) where p_bar is the geometric/arithmetic mean over views (or pairwise KL_S to the EN view as teacher). (3) Annealing: lambda = 0 for the first epoch, then ramp up (Asai & Hajishirzi; Li et al.) because early predictions are noisy. Can also run xTune-style 'model consistency': a second stage regularised toward a frozen first-stage model on augmented views.
params: Adds no parameters; backbone-dependent (184M-560M for typical encoders; LoRA-tuned LLMs also compatible).
compute: Requires all views of a pair in the same batch: 2 orders x up to 9 language combinations = up to 18 short sequences per source pair, so batches should be built by pair_id (e.g. 8-16 source pairs x 18 views). Total training examples equal the full T1+T2+T3+T4 training set (~27k rows), which is still small: base models fine-tune in ~10-20 min and large (435-560M) models in ~1 h on one 24 GB GPU with short sequences; no multi-GPU needed. Extra overhead vs plain CE is only the KL computation (negligible).
sample_efficiency: Well suited to ~1.3k reversible source pairs: the consistency terms exploit the within-pair structure (up to 18 correlated views per pair) as extra, label-free supervision. Li et al. 2019 find that the mirrored-instance loss reduces symmetry violations strongly even with 1% of SNLI/MNLI, and that lambda for the mirrored data can be ~1 while losses on unlabeled data need much smaller lambda at low data; too-large lambda can collapse predictions toward one class (they observed a drift to Neutral), the analogous risk here is drift toward EQ or NEG. Seed variance on this data size should be expected to be about 1-2 F1; regularisation typically reduces it slightly [uncertain].
reported_results: Reversal/symmetry: Li et al. 2019 BERT-base on SNLI+MNLI: symmetry violation rho_S 18.1% -> 6.2% (mirrored loss) -> 1.4% (+100k unlabeled mirrored pairs); conditional tau_S 59.6% -> 25.5-28.1%; accuracy unchanged or slightly up (SNLI 90.1 -> 90.2-90.5; MNLI 83.5 -> 84.1-84.3). At 5% data: rho_S 25.3% -> 3.2-7.1%. Asai & Hajishirzi 2020 (RoBERTa): WIQA 74.9 -> 77.0 acc with violations 12.0% -> 5.8%; QuaRel 81.1 -> 85.1, violations 19.2% -> 10.3%; +12-14 points with 20% of the data. Cross-lingual: xTune (Zheng et al. 2021) XNLI with XLM-R-large 79.2 -> 82.6 (zero-shot transfer, code-switch augmentation) and 82.6 -> 84.8 (translate-train-all, MT augmentation); XLM-R-base translate-train-all 78.8 -> 80.6, with example consistency alone giving 80.5; removing stop-gradient costs ~0.5; plain MT data augmentation without KL 78.8 vs 79.7 with example-consistency KL on the same data.
pilot_dico_results: Not evaluated in the LREC 2026 pilot (vanilla fine-tuning only; best DeBERTa-v3-base 0.75 W-F1 / 0.84 SoftCons / 0.79 HardCons on English; no multilingual experiments).
negative_other_handling: NEG stays an ordinary class inside the 4-way softmax; the reversal term maps NEG to itself, so it encourages p(NEG|a,b) = p(NEG|b,a) and hence symmetric NEG decisions, but does not forbid predicting NEG on a gold-reversible pair. Because NEG items are singletons in train/dev, the swapped NEG view must be synthesised (safe if non-reversible PhrasIS relations are order-invariant [uncertain]). A NEG threshold (or logit bias) should still be tuned on dev for weighted F1. The cross-lingual term makes NEG decisions agree across languages of the same pair.
metric_tradeoff: SoftCons: large improvement but not a hard guarantee (residual violations typically a few percent, per Li et al.); best combined with joint decoding or architectural symmetrisation to close the rest. HardCons: improves because consistent pairs are more often both right. Weighted F1: neutral to modestly positive (literature shows 0 to +2 accuracy for symmetry losses and +1.8-3.4 on XNLI for cross-lingual KL); main risk is over-regularisation (lambda too high) that smooths predictions toward a majority class and hurts FE/BE recall.
integration: Pure training-loop change: (1) a pair-grouped sampler keyed on pair_id that yields all views (twins via reverse_instance_id, and cross-language views via the shared pair_id) in the same batch; (2) a loss function in src/modules/loss.py computing CE + symmetric KL between log_softmax(z_x) and log_softmax(z_x_rev)[..., REVERSE_PERM] (with .detach() on targets), plus the view-mean KL in canonical orientation (use is_flipped() to decide whether to permute); (3) lambda warm-up callback. Backbone can stay HF AutoModelForSequenceClassification with num_labels=4.
ensemble_compatibility: Yes; produces standard 4-way probabilities, typically better calibrated across views and orders, which makes downstream joint decoding and cross-view log-prob pooling more reliable. Temperature scaling on dev still recommended since KL terms can sharpen or flatten distributions.
inference_cost: Zero extra inference cost (training-only regulariser): one forward pass per test row, seconds to minutes for ~4k rows per track on one GPU.
rules_disclosure: Disclose as a training objective (fine-tuning with consistency regularisation), the backbone access regime and architecture family, and that the multilingual training data of other tracks (same source pairs in EN/ES/EU) was used jointly. Using all official train files across tracks is organizer-provided data, not external data [uncertain whether organizers consider cross-track training data 'external' for a given track; it is expected to be fine].
contamination: No new data introduced. Joint cross-track training is leakage-free because splits are grouped by source pair across all tracks and languages (per task description). Backbone pretraining contamination is unchanged.
structural_cue_dependence: Training-time only: uses pair_id and twin ids to form views during training (fully available in train/dev). No dependence at test time, so behaviour is unaffected if test metadata differs.
expected_gain: On top of a multilingual cross-encoder trained on all tracks: SoftCons +0.05-0.12 before any decoding step, HardCons +0.02-0.05, W-F1 +0.5-2 points, with the largest W-F1 gains expected on T3 EU and T4 mixed through cross-lingual agreement [uncertain]. If joint decoding or architectural symmetrisation is already used, the incremental SoftCons benefit shrinks to ~0 (already guaranteed), and the value comes from better shared representations (W-F1/HardCons +0.5-1.5) [uncertain].
